key_insight: Introducing global scene tokens that provide scene-level awareness lets a feed-forward network allocate 3D Gaussian splats holistically, yielding compact representations with much faster, high-fidelity rendering than prior local or iterative allocation methods.
problem_solved: How to efficiently allocate and parametrize 3D Gaussian primitives for splatting so as to balance representation compactness, reconstruction fidelity, and fast (feed‑forward) inference without costly iterative optimization or local, myopic heuristics.
method: Encode multi-view inputs into a small set of learned global scene tokens (attention/aggregation over views) that capture global geometry and appearance context.

Decode those tokens in a feed-forward pass to predict splat parameters (positions, covariances, colors, importance) and a compact spatial allocation, with sparsity/compactness priors and optional lightweight refinement.
Train end-to-end with a differentiable splatting renderer and reconstruction losses so the tokens learn to allocate splats where they maximize fidelity and efficiency.
impact: Enables fast, scalable 3D reconstruction and real-time rendering workflows with far fewer primitives and no iterative optimization — useful for neural rendering, AR/VR, and large-scale scene capture pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-view encoder → global scene tokens → splat generator → differentiable splatting renderer
Allocation heatmap comparison: local/heuristic vs. GlobalSplat token-driven allocation (shows fewer, better-placed splats)
Speed vs. quality chart: rendering latency and memory vs. PSNR/LPIPS for GlobalSplat vs. iterative and prior feed‑forward baselines
Side-by-side renderings: input views, reconstructed images, and zoomed detail to illustrate fidelity with compact representation
paper_title: GlobalSplat: Efficient Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting via Global Scene Tokens
paper_authors: Roni Itkin, Noam Issachar, Yehonatan Keypur, Yehonatan Keypur, Anpei Chen
